title: Quantitative Optical Microscopy: Measurement of Cellular Biophysical Features with a Standard Optical Microscope
protocol: Open the SlideBook software and create a new slide for image collection.
Next, open the Focus Window in the SlideBook software.
Select DIC under the Filter Set section.
On the Scope tab, adjust the Aperture slide bar to the furthest right position (open all the way).
Focus on the sample using a DIC objective.
Adjust the halogen lamp intensity until the sample is easily visible.
Select the Camera tab in the Focus Window and check that the histogram of pixel intensities is within the dynamic range of the camera.
Open the Image Capture window.
In the Capture Type section, check the 3D box.
In the 3D Capture section, select the Range around center and Return to current location boxes.
Specify the Z-direction range, number of planes, and step size.
Check the DIC box in the Filter Set section.
Specify exposure time for DIC capture.
Name the image (optional).
Select Start to initiate DIC Z-stack imaging.
Open the Focus Window after completing DIC Z-stack acquisition.
Adjust the Aperture slide bar to the furthest left position.
Change the microscope light-path filter to green.
Adjust the halogen lamp intensity until the sample is visible without saturation.
Check the histogram of pixel intensities in the Camera tab for appropriate range.
Return to the Image Capture window and check the 3D Capture settings from DIC Z-stack acquisition.
In the Filter Set section, check the OPEN box.
Specify exposure time for Bright Field capture.
Name the image (optional).
Select Start to initiate BF Z-stack image acquisition.
Open a Z-stack capture.
Change the view to 100%.
Adjust the histogram of the pixel values to be displayed between 0 and the maximum pixel value of the camera.
Select View > Export > TIFF Series.
Save the TIFF series in a separate folder with a name that has an underscore at the end.
Repeat this with each DIC or BF Z-stack.
Open the HTDIC MATLAB program entitled "JoVE_HTDIC_v1.m".
Under Section 0 of the HTDIC program, update the dependencies directory variable.
Copy and paste the directory containing the hilbert_transform_dic.m and sobel_edge_detect.m files from explorer in between the single quotes following "dependencies_directory =".
Execute Section 0 of the JoVE_HTDIC_v1.m program.
In Section 1, update the "images_directory".
Again, copy and paste the directory containing the through-focus images in .tif form in between the single quotes.
ONLY RUN SECTION 1 ONCE.
Run Section 2 of the code.
Enter the focal plane number where the DIC image is in focus.
Input the lateral resolution (μm/pixel).
Specify the axial resolution (0.1 for acquisition in 0.1 μm steps).
Enter the rotation angle for the Hilbert transform (typical values are 45 and -135).
Define the region of interest size (typical value is 400).
Click Ok.
Position the blue box over the feature of interest, such as a cell.
Double-click inside the positioned box to proceed.
Adjust the contrast so dark features appear on the left and bright features on the right.
Drag the blue box over the desired region, reshape as necessary.
Run Section 3 to generate a mask for the z-stack cube.
Uncomment line 167 in the program.
Comment out line 170.
Execute Section 3 of the program.
Click and drag the mouse to define a rectangular mask.
Double-click on the box to accept it.
Comment out line 167 in the program.
Uncomment line 170.
Execute Section 3 of the program.
Click and draw the desired mask with the mouse.
Double-click on the mask to accept it.
Set "maskON" to 1 at line 179.
Run Section 4 to construct the Hilbert transformed DIC image stack.
Run Section 4 to construct the corresponding DIC image stack of the area of interest.
Run Section 5 to optimize the image segmentation of the xz cross sectional images of the region of interest.
Adjust the value of threshold and rerun this section until proper outlining is achieved in one of the columns.
If the optimal results are found in column 1, use Section 6 to determine the volume using DIC image segmentation.
If the optimal results are found in column 2, run Section 7 to determine cell volume from Hilbert-transformed DIC imagery.
If the optimal results are found in column 3, run Section 8 to determine volume using Fourier-filtered Hilbert-transformed DIC imagery.
Open the NIQPM MATLAB program entitled "JoVE_NIQPM_v1.m".
Update the location of three directories under Section 0: dependencies_directory, brightfield_directory, and dic_directory.
Run Section 1 to generate a bright field image cube of the full field of the entire set of images.
Run Section 2 in the software interface.
Enter the focal plane number where the bright field image is in focus.
Input lateral resolution (μm/pixel) into the dialog box.
Specify axial resolution as 0.1 for image acquisition in 0.1 μm steps.
Define region of interest size, typically set to 200.
Click OK to proceed with the defined parameters.
Adjust focal plane number if the bright field image is not in focus and rerun Section 2.
Drag the blue box around the feature of interest on the bright field image.
Resize the blue box by selecting nodes and dragging them as necessary.
Double-click inside the box to accept its position and size.
Run Section 3 to construct a stack of bright field images cropped to the region of interest.
Run Section 4 to generate phase map, pseudo DIC image, and comparisons with bright field imagery and true DIC image.
